prompt: What does the lesson use as the test of a good component boundary?

choices.text: The number of lines in the file, which should stay under fifty
choices.why: Length is not the test; what the piece needs to know is.

choices.text: How many props it needs, and whether it reaches into the page's variables
choices.why: Right. Three or four is a good cut; ten, or reaching into the page, is the wrong place.

choices.text: Whether it has its own `<style>` block
choices.why: Styles stay scoped either way; they do not decide the cut.

choices.text: Whether it could be reused on another page of the app
choices.why: Reuse is welcome, but `CourseList` is used once and is still a good cut.

prompt: How many props does the first version of `CourseList` declare?
hint: Courses, minutes, which one, and a way to say.

prompt: A student presses `Spanish`. In the first version, who changes `selected`?

choices.text: `CourseList`, by assigning to its prop
choices.why: That is the `$bindable` version, later in the lesson.

choices.text: The page, in the function it passed as `onselect`
choices.why: Right. The list only reports the choice.

choices.text: Svelte, which copies the clicked id into every component
choices.why: Nothing is copied automatically; the page assigns it.

choices.text: The button element itself, through its `aria-pressed` attribute
choices.why: `aria-pressed` only shows the state; it does not set it.

prompt: The planner's default shape: data goes down as props, and choices go ___ through callbacks.
What does `bind:value={date}` on an input do?

choices.text: Shows `date` in the field, and nothing more
choices.why: That is `value={date}`; the binding also writes back.

choices.text: Copies what was typed into `date` when the form is submitted
choices.why: It updates as you type, with no submit involved.

choices.text: Shows `date`, and typing changes `date`
choices.why: Right: one attribute, both directions.

choices.text: Validates the date and refuses anything that is not a real day
choices.why: Binding does no validation; the button's `disabled` is the only guard here.

prompt: The `Minutes` field holds 30 and is bound with `bind:value`. What is `minutes + 15`?
hint: What type does a number field's binding give?

choices.why: Right. On `type="number"` the binding gives a number.

choices.text: `"3015"`, because the browser holds the field as text
choices.why: The browser does, but Svelte converts it for a number field.

choices.text: `NaN`, since a field cannot hold a number
choices.why: The binding converts the text to a number.

choices.text: `null`, until the form has been submitted once
choices.why: `null` is only for an empty field.

prompt: After the form added 45 minutes on 21 October, how many minutes did Linear algebra have that week?
Match each binding with what its variable holds.
hint: One gives an element, not a value.

prompt: After `Add session`, the fields still show the date and 45. Why?

choices.text: The page sends the values back down to the form after adding
choices.why: The page passes the form nothing but `onadd`.

choices.text: The fields are the form's own state, and nothing cleared them
choices.why: Right. The page only received a copy.

choices.text: Bound fields cannot be cleared from code
choices.why: Assigning `date = ''` would clear it; nobody did.

prompt: The tempting `AddSession` pushed into the page's `sessions` and changed `same.minutes`. What did the console show?

choices.text: `ownership_invalid_mutation` for both changes
choices.why: Neither was caught: the check only sees assignments through the prop itself.

choices.text: An error, and the second session was not added
choices.why: Both changes worked; the 24th went to 90 minutes.

choices.text: Nothing beyond Vite's own two lines about connecting to the server
choices.why: Right, which is why the rule matters more than the warning.

choices.text: A warning for the `push` only, since it grew the array
choices.why: Growing the array is exactly what the check does not see.

prompt: Which line would trigger `ownership_invalid_mutation` in a child that received `sessions` as an unbound prop?
hint: It fires when assigning through the prop itself.

choices.text: `sessions.push(newSession)`
choices.why: The lesson's capture showed a push passing silently.

choices.text: `sessions[0].minutes += 30`
choices.why: Right: an assignment written against the prop.

choices.text: `const same = sessions.find(fn); same.minutes += 30`
choices.why: Through a local variable, which the check does not follow.

choices.text: `let total = sessions.length`
choices.why: Reading is never a mutation.

prompt: Why should only the page change `sessions`, even when a child's change works?
hint: Think of the day ids come from somewhere else.

choices.text: Because a child's change is lost on the next page load
choices.why: Every change is lost on reload here; that is not the difference.

choices.text: Because children run before the page and see old values
choices.why: Order is not the issue; ownership is.

choices.text: So that how a session is made is decided in one place
choices.why: Right. The owner of a piece of state should be the only code that changes its shape.

choices.text: Because Svelte refuses to compile a child that mutates a prop
choices.why: It compiled and ran; that is the trap.

prompt: The development warning for a child assigning through a prop it was not given to bind is `ownership_invalid____`.
hint: What the child did to the state.

prompt: What does `selected = $bindable()` in `CourseList`'s `$props` do?

choices.text: Lets the parent bind `selected`, so the child's assignments reach it
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: Makes `selected` required
choices.why: It says nothing about whether the prop is passed.

choices.text: Turns `selected` into state owned by the child, hidden from the parent
choices.why: The opposite: it shares the value with the parent.

choices.text: Gives `selected` a default of `undefined`
choices.why: A default goes in the parentheses; this is about binding.

prompt: `$bindable` was taken out and the page kept `bind:selected`. After pressing `Guitar`, what did `look` show?
hint: Compare the list with the heading below it.

choices.text: An error naming the prop that was not bindable
choices.why: There was no error and no warning.

choices.text: Guitar selected everywhere, as before
choices.why: The page's heading stayed on Linear algebra.

choices.text: Guitar pressed in the list, Linear algebra's sessions below
choices.why: Right: a silent disagreement.

choices.text: Nothing pressed at all, since the click was refused
choices.why: The child's own `selected` changed, so Guitar was pressed.

prompt: Match each planner component with how it reports to the page.
Why does `AddSession` stay a callback rather than a binding?
hint: What does the page do with what it receives?

choices.text: Because forms are not allowed to use `$bindable`
choices.why: Nothing forbids it; it is a design choice.

choices.text: Because a binding would make the page re-render on every keystroke
choices.why: Pages do not re-render whole in Svelte.

choices.text: Adding a session is the page's decision, not a value it stores
choices.why: Right. A callback reports what was asked; the page decides.

prompt: A `ul` rule sits in `CourseList`'s `<style>`. Which lists does it style?

choices.text: Every `ul` on the page
choices.why: Selectors are rewritten to require the component's class.

choices.text: The `ul` that `CourseList` writes
choices.why: Right. The session list is untouched.

choices.text: Every `ul` inside `CourseList` and inside its parent page
choices.why: Scoping does not extend to the parent.

choices.text: None, until the rule is wrapped in `:global`
choices.why: `:global` widens a rule; without it the rule still styles its own markup.

prompt: In the `curl` count, how many elements carried the `done` class?
Why does `CourseList` style `button[aria-pressed='true']` instead of a `.selected` class?

choices.text: Attribute selectors are faster than class selectors
choices.why: Speed is not the argument.

choices.text: Scoped styles cannot select on classes
choices.why: They can; the page uses `.done`.

choices.text: What is seen and what is announced cannot disagree
choices.why: Right. One attribute drives both.

choices.text: `.selected` would be refused by the compiler as an unused selector, every time
choices.why: Only when nothing uses it, which is a different point.

prompt: A rule that can never match any element of the component gets the warning `css_unused____`.
What is `bind:selected` short for?

choices.text: `selected={selected}`, a plain prop
choices.why: That is what `{selected}` is short for; it goes one way only.

choices.text: `bind:selected={selected}`, binding the page's variable of the same name
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: `onselect={(id) => (selected = id)}`
choices.why: That callback does the same job, but it is not what the shorthand stands for.

choices.text: `$bindable(selected)` inside the child
choices.why: The child declares `$bindable`; the shorthand is written in the parent.

choices.why: `onadd` is passed from the start.

choices.text: `minutes` is 30, below the field's minimum
choices.why: The minimum is 5.

` are disabled by default

prompt: When does the lesson say you need `:global(...)`?

choices.text: For any rule that uses an attribute selector
choices.why: `button[aria-pressed='true']` is scoped and works.

choices.text: When a selector must reach outside the component
choices.why: Right, as the layout does in lesson 12 for base styles.

choices.text: To stop the compiler from removing a rule it thinks is unused
choices.why: The lesson's fix for an unused rule is to delete it.

prompt: Put the lesson's changes to the planner in order.
items: `AddSession` with bound fields, and checkboxes in the page
trap: The binding replaced a callback that already existed, so the callback came first.

prompt: Which of these changes does the lesson consider the child's to make? Choose all that apply.
hint: Its own state, and what it was allowed to bind.

choices.text: `AddSession` changing its own `date`
choices.why: Yes: the form's state is the form's.

choices.text: `CourseList` assigning `selected` when the page bound it
choices.why: Yes: that is what `$bindable` offers.

choices.text: `AddSession` pushing into the page's `sessions`
choices.why: No: it works, silently, and takes a decision from the page.

choices.text: `WeekNav` assigning to its plain `week` prop to move the week
choices.why: No: the page would never see it; `WeekNav` calls `onchange`.
